weather_report:
Late morning in Subiaco arrives with the streets still damp from a passing shower, the sky a quilt of soft greys that lets the light through in hesitant patches. It feels calm rather than cold, the kind of cool-to-mild spring air that carries the smell of wet eucalyptus and fresh asphalt. Sunshine stays shy for now, but the clouds are thinning; by early afternoon expect broken cover and brighter spells that give the day a silvery sheen. When the sun pushes through, the UV will jump quickly for the season, so treat the light with respect even if the sky looks half-closed. Clarity will be mixed: slightly muted horizons this morning, then cleaner edges after lunchtime as the ceiling lifts.

It’s a day for simple comforts and unhurried errands. Wear breathable layers with a light waterproof at hand, shoes that don’t mind a puddle, and tuck sunglasses and a dab of sunscreen in your bag for the clearer patches later. A late coffee under an awning suits the moment, followed by a short train or bus hop for groceries, then an afternoon stroll once the breaks in the cloud arrive. If you’re staying in, open a window during the lull and let the softened light sweep the room, then save the outdoor chores for the brighter midafternoon.
